title: Northern Ireland
description: Bank holidays in Northern Ireland, with Easter Sunday

festivals.name: New Year’s Day
festivals.meaning: A bank holiday in Northern Ireland since 1974. When it falls at a weekend, the next Monday is the holiday.

festivals.name: St Patrick’s Day
festivals.meaning: A bank holiday in Ireland since 1903, kept in Northern Ireland. When it falls at a weekend, the next Monday is the holiday.

festivals.name: Good Friday
festivals.meaning: Marks the crucifixion. A traditional holiday in Northern Ireland, older than the bank holidays.

festivals.name: Easter Sunday
festivals.meaning: The Christian feast of the resurrection, on the Sunday after the church's full moon on or after 21 March, so between 22 March and 25 April. It isn't a bank holiday, being a Sunday.

festivals.name: Easter Monday
festivals.meaning: One of the first bank holidays, set by the Bank Holidays Act 1871.

festivals.name: Early May bank holiday
festivals.meaning: Added in 1978. It moved to Friday 8 May in 2020 for the 75th anniversary of VE Day, and to Monday 8 May in 1995 for the 50th.

festivals.name: Spring bank holiday
festivals.meaning: Took the place of Whit Monday in 1971. It moved into June for Elizabeth II’s Golden, Diamond and Platinum Jubilees.

festivals.name: Battle of the Boyne (Orangemen’s Day)
festivals.meaning: Marks William III’s victory at the Boyne in 1690. A public holiday in Northern Ireland. When it falls at a weekend, the next Monday is the holiday.

festivals.name: Summer bank holiday
festivals.meaning: Moved from the first Monday in August in 1971.

festivals.name: Christmas Day
festivals.meaning: A traditional holiday, older than the bank holidays. When it falls at a weekend, a weekday is given in its place.

festivals.name: Boxing Day
festivals.meaning: A bank holiday since 1871. When it falls at a weekend, a weekday is given in its place.

festivals.name: Silver Jubilee bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the Queen’s Silver Jubilee.

festivals.name: Royal wedding bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the wedding of Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer.

festivals.name: Millennium bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday to mark the new millennium.

festivals.name: Golden Jubilee bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the Queen’s Golden Jubilee, next to the moved spring bank holiday.

festivals.name: Royal wedding bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton.

festivals.name: Diamond Jubilee bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the Queen’s Diamond Jubilee, next to the moved spring bank holiday.

festivals.name: Platinum Jubilee bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the Queen’s Platinum Jubilee, next to the moved spring bank holiday.

festivals.name: State Funeral of Queen Elizabeth II
festivals.meaning: A one-off bank holiday for the Queen’s state funeral.

festivals.name: Coronation of King Charles III
festivals.meaning: A one-off bank holiday for the coronation, two days after it.
